column1: # DEFAULTS IN EVERY ORDER. The meet is commutative and associative, so every
# order of the same statements answers alike, and a concrete value beats a
# default of either rank whichever side it arrives on. Each family is one set
# of statements written in every order, its rows named by that order, one
# letter per statement as the family's comment spells them. defaults.tsv
# states the rules, R5 among them; these rows hold that no order escapes them.
# toggle: p the spread `e: &: { active: **true | boolean }`, v the value
# `e: x: active: true`, s the stronger default `e: x: active: *false |
# boolean`: a project switching on what its template defaults off.

column3: e: &: { active: **true | boolean }\ne: x: active: true\ne: x: active: *false | boolean
e: &: { active: **true | boolean }\ne: x: active: *false | boolean\ne: x: active: true
e: x: active: true\ne: &: { active: **true | boolean }\ne: x: active: *false | boolean
e: x: active: true\ne: x: active: *false | boolean\ne: &: { active: **true | boolean }
e: x: active: *false | boolean\ne: &: { active: **true | boolean }\ne: x: active: true
e: x: active: *false | boolean\ne: x: active: true\ne: &: { active: **true | boolean }
